coverage_notes: All 162 cross-module module-attribute candidate groups and all 28 cross-module regex sigil groups have source-consumer assessments. The parse-only inline census covers 32745 scalar leaves in all 1032 frozen src/lib Elixir files. The 191 high-fanout value groups have lexical/source-role screens. A type-preserving lower-fanout index records all 1514 other cross-module values: 316/738 long strings and 63/67 numbers have bounded source-context screens; the 709 short strings have a source-role ledger with 261 classified as existing overlap, syntax, display/log or external protocol/path tokens. Exactly 422 long strings, 448 short strings and four generic zero/one numeric forms remain without semantic caller review. Screens do not prove transitive equivalence. Dynamic Regex.compile, generated code and non-Elixir files remain outside this detector. Equal values are not counted as independent extraction opportunities or savings.

findings.title: Ordered priced token dimensions repeat across usage owners
findings.description: Four identical five-element lists define the priced/reconciled dimension order. UsageEnvelope derives that subset from six raw fields, and Pricing.Components uses order in zero-value selection. A single low-dependency owner is plausible. This corroborates telemetry-usage-34; it is not a separate estimated saving and must preserve provider-specific admission.
findings.recommendation: Share the ordered priced-dimension vocabulary below the envelope and pricing layers; keep raw-total and provider/component policies separate.

findings.title: Model catalog refresh budget mirrors the CLI probe budget
findings.description: Both attributes use 20,000 ms and ModelDiscovery comments that refresh_now matches the CLI probe timeout. Since the refresh wraps the probe, equal numeric values leave no explicit allowance for setup/cleanup overhead. Source alone does not demonstrate a timeout incident.
findings.recommendation: Define the nested budget relationship explicitly and test boundary timing with an injected slow probe before choosing one owner or changing the values.

findings.title: Build Order draft-body byte cap is repeated at load and record boundaries
findings.description: PlanningSource accepts a pack document body only when its byte size is 1..64,000; Member.new then applies the same range to draft_body. The two checks are the same Build Order draft-body contract at adjacent boundaries. The path-containment check and record validation serve separate purposes, so only the byte cap is a shared policy candidate. No production incidence or LOC saving is measured.
findings.recommendation: Give the Build Order draft-body bound one low-dependency owner and retain both read and record checks.

findings.title: Provider active-turn error code is recognized in two queue recovery paths
findings.description: Both paths recognize JSON-RPC code -32,003 as a provider active-turn rejection and restore durable queue work, but they receive different outer error tuples and call different restoration APIs. A named provider error recognizer can prevent one path drifting if the protocol code changes; it must not merge the two delivery decisions or alter their item state transitions. The checkpoint path explicitly describes this as defensive parity with turn-boundary drain. Agent-runtime-09 already identifies this backend protocol leak, so this is corroborating constant-level evidence rather than an independent defect.
findings.recommendation: Own the active-turn code in the provider error contract while preserving each caller's tuple matching and restoration policy.

findings.title: Dashboard advertised-host fallback is repeated for control URLs
findings.description: HttpServer.display_host/1 and PaneManager.Anchor.control_url_host/0 both map wildcard, empty and nil dashboard bind hosts to 127.0.0.1 before advertising a reachable URL. HttpServer also stringifies other host values, while Anchor only handles binaries; sharing a policy must preserve or explicitly resolve that input difference. The string match is a local source contract, not evidence of a measured operator failure or LOC saving.
findings.recommendation: Define an advertised-dashboard-host policy below both URL publishers, with a tested nonbinary input contract.
